'''''Sedum dasyphyllum''''',<ref>[http://www.desert-tropicals.com/Plants/Crassulaceae/Sedum_dasyphyllum.html ''Sedum dasyphyllum'' at desert-tropicals.com]</ref><ref>{{in lang|fr}} [http://www.tela-botanica.org/eflore/BDNFF/4.02/nn/62201 ''Sedum dasyphyllum'' on tela-botanica.org]</ref> also named '''''Sedum burnatii''''' and commonly known as '''Corsican stonecrop'''<ref name="Ondra2007">{{cite book|author=Nancy J. Ondra|title=Foliage: Astonishing Color and Texture Beyond Flowers|url=https://archive.org/details/foliageastonishi0000ondr|url-access=registration|accessdate=2 September 2012|date=15 April 2007|publisher=Storey Publishing|isbn=978-1-58017-648-4|page=[https://archive.org/details/foliageastonishi0000ondr/page/177 177]}}</ref> or '''thick-leaved stonecrop''',<ref>[http://www.maltawildplants.com/CRSS/Sedum_dasyphyllum.php Thick-leaved Stonecrop page on maltawildplants.com]</ref> is a low-growing [[succulent plant|succulent]] [[flowering plant]] of the genus ''[[Sedum]]'' in the family [[Crassulaceae]].

==Description==
It is a small perennial plant with green-turquoise or gray-green opposite leaves and a creeping [[Plant stem|stem]] forming shrubs.<ref>[http://www.backyardgardener.com/plantname/pd_ecdd.html ''Sedum dasyphyllum'' on backyardgardner.com]</ref> Its flowers are white and small with little black dots on the [[petal]]s and green ovaries. The ''Sedum dasyphyllum'', typical of the [[Mediterranean Basin|Mediterranean region]], usually grows among the rocks, especially among the [[tuff]] walls of rural areas.
